title: Edit mode very slow on large documents: hover on floating menu/toolbar and opening a block editor lag
body:
## Symptom On a large MyST chapter the preview is very slow in edit mode, while scrolling stays fluid: 1. hovering the floating menu (block palette / insert bar), 2. opening a block editor (click on a block), 3. hovering the edit toolbar, 4. typing in an open block editor. Reproduction document: `book/chapters/08-research-plan-implement.md` of the Agentic Coding White Paper (110 KB, 2403 lines, 709 mapped blocks). Version 1.9.1 (`495e4710`). ### What makes this document unusual Compared with the next two largest chapters, which are 72 KB and 69 KB and feel fine: | Metric | ch. 08 | ch. 02 | ch. 09 | |---|---|---|---| | Pipe-table rows | **230** | 30 | 29 | | `{table}` directives | **17** | 0 | 0 | | `
` inside table cells | **65** | – | – | | Directives | **70** | 58 | 24 | | `{cite}` roles | **96** | 41 | 65 | | `{figure}` (external SVG ``) | 23 | 28 | 12 | | mermaid / PlantUML / math | 0 | 0 | 0 | The main structural outlier is the large number of tables. Rendered page: ~690 KB of HTML. ## Measurements (headless Chromium, built `preview.js`, CDP profiler) The webview page was rebuilt standalone from the 08 chapter. This bench has **no** VS Code webview, **no** images loaded, no comments and no side-by-side or incoming marks. | Interaction | ch. 11 (19 KB, 120 blocks) | ch. 08 (110 KB, 709 blocks) | Dominant cost | |---|---|---|---| | Hover on floating menu / toolbar (160 moves) | 5 ms | 9 ms | `closest` | | Hover over blocks in edit mode (240 moves) | 37 ms | 67 ms | `getBoundingClientRect`, `querySelectorAll` | | **Open a block editor** | 37 ms | **90 ms** | forced synchronous layout | | Typing (per key) | – | 0.8 ms | `getBoundingClientRect` | | Toggle edit mode | – | 58 ms | layout reads | | Content patch (page side) | 15 ms | 53 ms | morph + `replaceChildren` | On the host, one edit costs about 190 ms per round trip on ch. 08: - `renderMyst`: 86 ms, of which parse 30 ms and to-HTML 45 ms. - `buildPreviewWebviewHtml`: 18 ms. - `planContentPatch` (parse5 of the whole page): 29 ms. Host cost grows linearly with document size (25/50/100/200/400 % → 13/48/86/129/251 ms). Tables and directives dominate the render. Removing all pipe tables halves it; `{cite}` roles have no measurable impact. **The bench does not reproduce the multi-hundred-millisecond lag felt in VS Code.** The cost that is missing is therefore most likely layout, style recalculation or paint work. That work scales with the size of the DOM and is amplified in the real webview: images, VS Code CSS, devicePixelRatio and GPU compositing. ## Suspects (static audit + profiles) Confirmed in the profile (opening a block editor scales with document size): - Right after the editor DOM is inserted, the scroll-anchor code (`page/features/scrollCore.ts`) reads `getBoundingClientRect().top`, which forces a full-page layout (≈18 ms on ch. 08). - Palette positioning, called from `receiveBlockEditSource` (`page/features/editorChrome.ts`), reads `palette.element.getBoundingClientRect()` and forces another layout (≈13 ms). Plausible, and needing a trace in the real webview: - **Style recalc on hover over a large DOM.** - `editMode.ts:265-272` writes `data-sphinx-preview-edit-hover` on every `mouseover`/`mouseout`. - `core/preview/styles/*` contain about 25 `:has()` rules (`contentLayoutStyles.ts:67,76`, `contentBlockStyles.ts:19,121`, `codeBlockStyles.ts:31+`). - Edit mode also has sibling-hover rules (`[data-sphinx-source-line]:hover + .sphinx-preview-insert-point …`, `editModeStyles.ts:135,147,175`, and `tbody tr:hover` in `tableStyles.ts:73`). - Edit mode adds an insert bar and move buttons after every block (`insertPoints.ts:105-160`), which multiplies the node count. - **Repaint of the 23 SVG `` figures** when a high-level attribute or class changes. This was not measured, because the bench loaded no images. - **Layout thrash per table:** `page/modules/widthMode.ts:231-298` (`measureWide`/`planTable`) interleaves writes (probe, `data-sphinx-preview-measuring`) with `getBoundingClientRect` reads, once per table. 17+ tables on ch. 08 means N forced reflows. It runs after each patch, from `stabilizeLayout`, and from the `MutationObserver` on `data-sphinx-preview-editing` (`widthMode.ts:386-394`), so it fires when an editor opens or closes. - **Content `ResizeObserver` → `stabilizeLayout`** (`scrollCore.ts:573-575`, `:410-440`) runs on every height change of the content, including textarea autosize while typing. It calls `markWideTables`, `widthMode.update`, `measure` and `toc.remeasure`. - **`parseMappings` / `measureLineTops`** (`scrollCore.ts:96-150`) create one `Range` per character of multi-line paragraphs and call `getClientRects` on each one. - **`firstClearance`** (`page/modules/firstClearance.ts:326`) uses a `childList`/`subtree`/`characterData` observer on the whole content. A single change can start a per-frame `settle()` loop of up to 300 frames (`:289-300`). - **Per keystroke** (`blockSourceEditor.ts:334-358`): textarea autosize, then `getBoundingClientRect`, then `revealCaretBelowPalette` → `caretRectOf` (`modules/caretRect.ts`), which builds a mirror div and forces layout. This repeats on `keyup`, `mouseup` and `select`. - **`topLevelMappedBlocks()`** (`features/mappedBlocks.ts:34-47`) is rebuilt on every call: a `querySelectorAll`, an ancestor walk and a sort. It is used from hover paths such as `insertPoints.blockOfTarget`. ## Suggested next steps 1. Record a DevTools **Performance** trace in the real webview (*Developer: Open Webview Developer Tools*) on ch. 08 while hovering the floating menu and opening a block. Check whether the time goes to *Recalculate Style*, *Layout* or *Paint*, and which elements are invalidated. 2. Batch the layout reads in the editor-open path (anchor + palette) into one `requestAnimationFrame`, after all writes. 3. In `widthMode.measureWide`, do all writes, then all reads; skip tables whose geometry key did not change; ignore `data-sphinx-preview-editing` mutations that do not change widths. 4. Suspend or debounce `stabilizeLayout` and `firstClearance.settle` while a block editor is open. 5. Scope hover styling so it does not invalidate the whole content: avoid attribute writes on ancestors and avoid `:has()` on `#content`. Consider `content-visibility: auto` / `contain: layout style` on top-level blocks. 6. Cache `topLevelMappedBlocks` and the block geometry, and invalidate the cache on `contentReplaced`. 7. Add a large-document performance fixture (for example a copy of ch. 08) to the visual/e2e harness with a budget on *open block editor* and *hover* latency.
